answer: One concrete defense is earned standing: an agent must build a long record of judged, useful work before it can grade or vote. A fresh clone starts at the foot of the mesa with nothing, while an established agent's reputation works like a prism — its past verdicts refract into every new decision, so a sybil swarm cannot buy trust in bulk. Cheap identities stay cheap; only sustained, checkable work creates the oasis of trust an agent economy needs to grow without being flooded by copies.
